subject: MKL multithreaded library and mclapply do not play well together

messages.author: 6061a6b2b7a23d5d
messages.subject: MKL multithreaded library and mclapply do not play well together
parts:
After some testing, I have discovered that using mclapply on multiple cores with MKLthreads set to greater than 1 results in the threads sleeping and basically never finishing. Obviously, the temporary solution is to set MKLthreads to 1. But it would be nice if these functions worked together, because you cannot always guarantee that a package in R will not use mclapply while calling a MKL threaded math function, and there are situations where I would like to just use MKLthreads > 1 and not worry about it.

I am running Ubuntu 14.04 with RRO 3.2.1 and RStudio 0.99.486. I would upgrade to RRO 3.2.2, but it broke RStudio, so I downgraded.  I have an Intel 4-core processor with 2 threads per core.

Here is some code to test the problem:

library(parallel)
set.seed(1)
m <- 10000
n <- 2000
A <- matrix(runif (m*n),m,n)


setMKLthreads(1)
system.time(S <- svd (A,nu=0,nv=0))
# user  system elapsed
# 7.282   0.133   7.431


setMKLthreads(4)
system.time(S <- svd (A,nu=0,nv=0))
# user  system elapsed
# 16.584   0.347   5.377


setMKLthreads(1)
system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
                     FUN=svd,
                     nu=0,
                     nv=0,
                     mc.cores=4))
# user  system elapsed
# 852.845  35.167  19.691


setMKLthreads(4)
system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
                     FUN=svd,
                     nu=0,
                     nv=0,
                     mc.cores=1))
# user  system elapsed
# 66.333   1.245  21.573


setMKLthreads(4)
system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
                     FUN=svd,
                     nu=0,
                     nv=0,
                     mc.cores=4))
# threads sleep; use 0% cpu and do not finish

messages.author: 9ca0345d553844f2
messages.subject: Re: MKL multithreaded library and mclapply do not play well together
parts:
Hello,
I hope someone else will jump in on your mclapply issue, but the RStudio issue with RRO is likely fixable. Try the following:  As reported on Github, it may be related to the following: Line 4 in /usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib64/R/bin/R determines R_HOME_DIR based on readlink /proc/$$/fd/255. Since this command is implementation-dependent, it does not work the same way across each environment. Some users have had success by updating line 4 to use the absolute path to R such as: 
  • R_HOME_DIR=/usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib64/R 
  • R_HOME_DIR=/usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib/R
The actual path depends on your environment or distribution. Hope this helps.

Thanks,
Josée

messages.author: 149440eddb848db9
messages.subject: Re: MKL multithreaded library and mclapply do not play well together
parts:
Hi, Michael

I plan to write in more detail on this topic in a blog post early next week, but I want to respond with some quick thoughts:

  1. Most of the benefit of the MKL comes from fast vectorised math. The multithreaded computation adds a little bit to the performance, but in reality very little (see the performance benchmarks at https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/rro/multithread/#mt-bench).
  2. So, if you want to set and forget a setting, I suggest you use setMklthreads(1)
  3. Parallel programming in R is hard and full of pitfalls.  Your problem with parallel math is just one of these.  See paragraph 2, "A word of caution" in the doParallel vignette (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/doParallel/vignettes/gettingstartedParallel.pdf) that points out other pitfalls.


Regards


Andrie
